newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden approves parallel imports of Astra drug.
newsitem.headline: Sweden approves parallel imports of Astra drug.

text.p: Sweden's drugs administration, Lakemedelsverket, has approved parallel imports of drug company Astra's ulcer treatment Losec from other parts of Europe.
"The approval came through on Friday," Gunilla Edman-Bergstrand, a Lakemedelsverket spokeswoman, told Reuters.
Cross Pharma AB, which is the company that received the approval, will import Losec from Italy and initially sell it in hospitals in Sweden.
Parallel importing enables licenced companies to buy brand products in countries where prices are lowest and subsequently sell them on the local market at reduced prices.
Cross Pharma's director Freddie Norberg said the company has not yet set the price but said it could be 10 percent cheaper than the current price.
Norberg told Reuters that he did not think the parallel import would force Astra to lower its prices in Sweden.
But Astra spokesman Staffan Ternby said the approval would lead to lower price levels.
"You can expect this will have an effect on prices," Ternby told Reuters.

Ternby said parallel imports would probably result in a shift of the market from northern to southern Europe, where Losec is sold at lower prices. Astra has marketing companies in both Italy and Spain.
To date Losec is the only drug that has approval for parallel imports in Sweden, the state's drugs administration said.
"Losec is only the beginning," Norberg said. "We will start other drugs as well."
